findings.region: lead image / desktop and mobile first read
findings.observation: The 01 of 02 open-movie mark gives the lead image a concrete programme role and adds a subject-native cue without covering the characters.
findings.consequence: The opening is more identifiable at thumbnail size while the image remains the dominant object.
findings.repair: Keep the mark only while it remains legible at narrow widths and does not become a reusable decorative badge.

findings.observation: The reversed second screening still leaves a large white interval; the image and end date make the reversal legible, but the pause is quieter than the reference composition.
findings.consequence: The interval may read as empty layout space for some subjects even though it is comfortable for this small programme.
findings.repair: Keep this as a content-dependent option in the skill: use a cue only when the subject provides one, otherwise let the pause remain open rather than filling it with generic cards.

largestGap: The opening mark resolves the first-read specificity gap; the remaining wide-screen pause needs a subject-specific decision rather than a universal density rule.
nextOperation: Carry the mark and subject-material check into the Skill, then use a different one-sentence benchmark to test whether the rule adapts without forcing a film layout.
regressionCheck: Check 390x844, 320x740, actual detail/save/filter flows, and clean console logs after any future opening change.
